ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a broken-line graph of the function f; the broken line passes through the points (0,3), (3,6), and (6,0). At x=4, the graph is located on the descending straight-line segment from (3,6) to (6,0). Reasoning: The slope of the descending line segment is (0-6)/(6-3)=-2, so f'(4)=-2. Starting from (3,6), in the equation of this line segment, when x increases by 1, y decreases by 2; therefore when x=4, f(4)=4. Given h(x)=(x+1)f(x), using the product rule gives h'(x)=f(x)+(x+1)f'(x). Substituting x=4: h'(4)=f(4)+5f'(4)=4+5(-2)=-6.
